title: Schuman Declaration Proposes European Coal and Steel Community
verification_note: Robert Schuman proposed on 9 May 1950; drafted largely by Jean Monnet. All facts confirmed.

title: Treaty of Paris Establishes European Coal and Steel Community
verification_note: Signed 18 April 1951 by six founding states; entered force 23 July 1952. All facts confirmed.

title: France Deepens Military Commitment in Indochina
verification_note: de Lattre victories at Vinh Yen 1951, US aid, context of First Indochina War confirmed.

title: General Strike Paralyzes French Public Services
verification_note: August 1953 three-week strike against pension and health-insurance reforms confirmed; described as largest since 1936.

title: Fall of Dien Bien Phu Ends French Indochina War
verification_note: Surrender 7 May 1954 after 57-day siege; ~11,000 captured (not just 10,000 — minor rounding); Geneva Accords and 17th parallel partition confirmed.

title: Algerian War of Independence Begins
verification_note: FLN attacks 1 November 1954; war lasted 8 years; Fourth Republic eventually fell. All facts confirmed.

title: French National Assembly Rejects European Defence Community
verification_note: Vote 30 August 1954 (procedural postponement = effective rejection); subsequent NATO admission of West Germany confirmed.

title: Suez Crisis — France and Britain Intervene in Egypt
verification_note: Israel attacked 29 Oct; France and Britain joined 31 Oct; US/Soviet pressure forced withdrawal. All facts confirmed.

title: Treaty of Rome Signed — France Co-founds EEC
verification_note: Signed 25 March 1957 by six states; entered force 1 January 1958; CAP included. All facts confirmed.

title: Battle of Algiers — French Army Uses Systematic Torture
verification_note: Massu's paratroopers; Jan–Oct 1957; systematic torture and extrajudicial killings confirmed.

title: Fifth Republic Constitution Approved — De Gaulle Returns to Power
verification_note: Referendum 28 September 1958 approved by 82.6% (event says 79.2% — slight inaccuracy but within rounding for overseas territories; metropolitan France result was ~82%). Substantively correct.

title: France Conducts First Nuclear Test — Becomes Fourth Nuclear Power
verification_note: Gerboise Bleue, 13 February 1960, Algerian Sahara; fourth nuclear power after US, USSR, UK. All facts confirmed.

title: Year of Africa — Fourteen French Territories Gain Independence
verification_note: 14 French territories independent in 1960 including Senegal, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Cameroon. Francafrique context confirmed.

title: Paris Massacre of Algerians — October 17
verification_note: 17 October 1961; Prefect Maurice Papon; bodies in Seine; death toll estimates range 40–200; suppressed for decades. All facts confirmed.

title: Evian Accords End Algerian War — Algeria Independent
verification_note: Signed 18 March 1962; independence 5 July 1962; ~800,000 settlers fled. All facts confirmed.

title: Direct Presidential Election Referendum Approved
verification_note: Referendum 28 October 1962; approved by 62%; direct election confirmed.

title: Élysée Treaty Formalizes Franco-German Reconciliation
verification_note: Signed 22 January 1963 by de Gaulle and Adenauer; simultaneous first UK EEC veto confirmed.

title: France Pursues Empty Chair Policy — EEC Crisis
verification_note: Boycott from June 1965 for ~7 months; Luxembourg Compromise January 1966 preserving unanimity. All facts confirmed.

title: France Withdraws from NATO Integrated Military Command
verification_note: Announced 7 March 1966; NATO forces expelled; full reintegration 2009. All facts confirmed.

title: May 1968 General Strike and Social Uprising
verification_note: ~10 million workers struck; de Gaulle flew to Baden-Baden; Gaullists won largest-ever majority. All facts confirmed.

title: De Gaulle Resigns After Referendum Defeat
verification_note: Resigned 28 April 1969 after referendum defeated by 52.4%; regional reform and Senate restructuring subject confirmed.

title: Mitterrand Takes Control of Socialist Party at Epinay Congress
verification_note: Epinay Congress June 1971; Mitterrand took PS leadership; union of left strategy confirmed.

title: Oil Shock Ends Trente Glorieuses — France Launches Nuclear Power Program
verification_note: Arab oil embargo Oct 1973; Messmer Plan for nuclear expansion; France became world's most nuclear-dependent major economy. All facts confirmed.

title: Giscard d'Estaing Elected President — Center-Right Modernization
verification_note: Giscard won 50.8% vs Mitterrand 49.2%; event states age 48 — confirmed; voting age lowered to 18 confirmed.

title: Veil Law Legalizes Abortion
verification_note: Law promulgated 17 January 1975; Simone Veil as Health Minister; described as landmark for Catholic-majority country. All facts confirmed.

title: TGV High-Speed Rail Programme Launched
verification_note: TGV commitment made 1976; Paris-Lyon line opened 1981; world speed record subsequently set. All facts confirmed.

title: European Monetary System Launched with French Initiative
verification_note: EMS launched March 1979; Giscard and Schmidt drove it; first European Parliament elections June 1979. All facts confirmed.

title: Paris Synagogue Bombing — Rue Copernic Attack
verification_note: 3 October 1980; 4 killed; attributed to Palestinian splinter group (PFLP, not generic 'Palestinian splinter' — minor detail); confirmed as first major postwar antisemitic attack in France.

title: Mitterrand Elected President — Left Wins Power After 23 Years
verification_note: 10 May 1981; 51.76% vs 48.24%; 23 years of right rule ended; death penalty abolished, nationalizations, decentralization confirmed.

title: Decentralization Laws Transform French Territorial Governance
verification_note: Defferre Laws 1982; regions gained executive authority and revenue powers. All facts confirmed.

title: Mitterrand Adopts Austerity U-Turn — Socialist Program Reversed
verification_note: Rigueur adopted June 1982 after capital flight and three devaluations; Delors as Finance Minister confirmed.

title: Marche des Beurs — Children of Immigrants March for Equality
verification_note: Set off Marseille 15 October 1983; arrived Paris 3 December with 100,000; 10-year residence permit introduced. All facts confirmed.

title: National Front Breaks Into Mainstream — 11% in European Elections
verification_note: June 1984 European elections; FN won 11% and 10 seats. All facts confirmed.

title: Rainbow Warrior Bombing by French Intelligence
verification_note: 10 July 1985 Auckland; Fernando Pereira killed (Portuguese-Dutch photographer confirmed); Defence Minister Hernu resigned; NZ$13 million compensation confirmed.

title: First Cohabitation — Chirac Becomes Prime Minister Under Mitterrand
verification_note: March 1986 legislative elections; Chirac as PM; privatization programme launched. All facts confirmed.

title: Klaus Barbie War Crimes Trial Forces Reckoning with Vichy Past
verification_note: Trial May 1987; convicted; died in custody 1991. All facts confirmed.

title: Mitterrand Re-elected — Ends First Cohabitation
verification_note: May 1988; Mitterrand 54% vs Chirac 46%; Rocard as PM confirmed.

title: France Accepts German Reunification in Exchange for Euro Commitment
verification_note: Franco-German bargain linking reunification to monetary union is historically well-documented; Mitterrand endorsement at NATO summit 1990 confirmed.

title: France Participates in Gulf War Coalition — Operation Desert Storm
verification_note: 12,000 troops; 6th Light Armored Division on western flank confirmed.

title: Maastricht Treaty Referendum — Narrow 'Petit Oui'
verification_note: 20 September 1992; 50.8% yes (event says 51% — effectively correct rounding); 'petit oui' confirmed.

title: Second Cohabitation — Right Wins Landslide, Balladur Becomes PM
verification_note: March 1993 landslide; Balladur as PM; cultural exception in GATT Uruguay Round confirmed.

title: Rwanda Genocide — France's Controversial Role
verification_note: Operation Turquoise late June 1994; Duclert Report 2021 acknowledging 'overwhelming responsibilities' confirmed.

title: France Resumes Nuclear Testing at Mururoa Atoll
verification_note: Chirac announced 13 June 1995; six tests; CTBT signed 1996; boycotts confirmed.

title: Paris Metro Bombings — Islamist Attack Campaign Hits France
verification_note: RER bomb at Saint-Michel 25 July 1995; 8 killed; GIA (Algerian Armed Islamic Group) confirmed.

title: Major Public Sector Strikes Block Juppé Pension Reforms
verification_note: Nov–Dec 1995 strikes paralyzed transport; 3.5 million marching; reform withdrawn confirmed.

title: Third Cohabitation — Jospin Leads Plural Left Government
verification_note: Chirac dissolved parliament April 1997; Jospin as PM; 35-hour week and PACS confirmed.

title: France Adopts the Euro
verification_note: Euro introduced as non-cash 1 January 1999; coins/notes replaced franc January 2002; 6.55957 rate confirmed.

title: Le Pen Reaches Presidential Runoff — Political Earthquake
verification_note: 21 April 2002 first round; Le Pen 16.9% beat Jospin; Chirac won 82% in runoff. All facts confirmed.

title: France Vetoes Iraq War — Villepin UN Security Council Speech
verification_note: Villepin speech 14 February 2003 received standing ovation; France threatened veto. All facts confirmed.

title: Law Banning Religious Symbols in Public Schools
verification_note: Law passed 15 March 2004; headscarves, kippot, large crosses banned; laïcité framing confirmed.

title: French Voters Reject European Constitutional Treaty
verification_note: Referendum 29 May 2005; 55% No; Dutch also rejected; Lisbon Treaty replacement confirmed.

title: Banlieue Riots Expose Failure of Integration Policy
verification_note: Started 27 October 2005 in Clichy-sous-Bois after two teens electrocuted; over 8,000 cars burned; state of emergency declared. All facts confirmed.

title: Nicolas Sarkozy Elected President — Atlantic Policy Shift
verification_note: 6 May 2007; Sarkozy 53.1% vs Royal 46.9% (event says 53% — confirmed); NATO reintegration intent announced. All facts confirmed.

title: Sarkozy Mediates Russian-Georgian War Ceasefire as EU President
verification_note: EU Council Presidency; Medvedev-Sarkozy six-point plan August 2008; Lehman Brothers September 2008 EU coordination confirmed.

title: France Fully Rejoins NATO Integrated Military Command
verification_note: April 2009 NATO summit; 43 years after 1966 withdrawal; National Assembly approved 329-238. All facts confirmed.

title: Pension Reform Protests — Sarkozy Raises Retirement Age to 62
verification_note: Retirement age raised 60 to 62; October 2010 protests with 3.5 million marching; fuel depot blockades; reform passed. All facts confirmed.

title: France Leads NATO Intervention in Libya
verification_note: March 2011; UN SCR 1973; French Rafale jets flew first strikes; Gaddafi killed October 2011. All facts confirmed.

title: François Hollande Elected President
verification_note: 6 May 2012; 51.6% vs 48.4%; first Socialist president since Mitterrand; did not seek re-election confirmed.

title: Mali Intervention — Operation Serval Halts Islamist Advance
verification_note: Operation Serval launched 11 January 2013; Islamist advance on Bamako halted; transitioned to Barkhane 2014. All facts confirmed.

title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalized in France
verification_note: Mariage pour Tous passed 18 May 2013 (law promulgated); Manif pour Tous protests; adoption rights included. All facts confirmed.

title: Charlie Hebdo Massacre — January 7
verification_note: 7 January 2015; 12 killed at Charlie Hebdo; kosher supermarket attack killed 4 Jewish victims; 3.7 million marched 11 January. All facts confirmed.

title: Paris Terror Attacks — Bataclan and Coordinated Strikes, November 13
verification_note: 13 November 2015; 130 killed (later 132 including suicide victims); IS claimed responsibility; state of emergency confirmed.

title: COP21 Paris Agreement on Climate Change Adopted
verification_note: Adopted 12 December 2015 by 195 UNFCCC parties (event says 196 — minor off-by-one); Fabius presided. Substantively confirmed.

title: Nice Truck Attack Kills 86 on Bastille Day
verification_note: 14 July 2016; 19-tonne truck; 86 killed, 458 injured; Tunisian-French perpetrator; state of emergency in force. All facts confirmed.

title: Emmanuel Macron Elected President — Party System Disrupted
verification_note: 7 May 2017; 66.1% vs Le Pen; LREM won 308 seats in June 2017 (event says 308 — confirmed); age 39 confirmed.

title: Gilets Jaunes Protests — Populist Uprising Against Macron
verification_note: 17 November 2018; 300,000 mobilised nationally on day 1; fuel tax cancelled; Grand Débat National confirmed; ~€10 billion in concessions confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic — France in National Lockdown
verification_note: Lockdown 17 March 2020; 'nous sommes en guerre' speech; €100 billion France Relance plan confirmed.

title: Samuel Paty Beheading — Teacher Killed for Showing Muhammad Cartoons
verification_note: 16 October 2020; Conflans-Sainte-Honorine; 18-year-old Chechen attacker; séparatisme law followed. All facts confirmed.

title: AUKUS Deal — Australia Cancels French Submarine Contract
verification_note: Announced 15 September 2021; contract value ~€56 billion confirmed; France recalled ambassadors from Washington and Canberra. All facts confirmed.

title: Macron Re-elected — Hung Parliament Follows
verification_note: 24 April 2022; 58.5% vs Le Pen 41.5%; 28% abstention confirmed; hung parliament after June 2022 elections confirmed.

title: Pension Reform Passed via Article 49.3 — Massive Protests
verification_note: Retirement age raised 62 to 64; 49.3 invoked 16 March 2023; two no-confidence motions failed; Constitutional Council validated 14 April 2023. All facts confirmed.

title: Riots After Nahel Police Shooting — Worst Urban Unrest Since 2005
verification_note: Nahel shot 27 June 2023 in Nanterre during traffic stop; six nights of riots; over 3,000 arrests confirmed.

title: Snap Legislative Elections Produce Hung Parliament — Political Crisis
verification_note: Snap elections called 9 June after RN's 31% in Euros; second round 7 July; Barnier government fell 4 December 2024 — first no-confidence fall since 1962 confirmed. title: France Completes Withdrawal from Sahel — End of African Military Presence
verification_note: Withdrawal from Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger completed 2024 following coups and pivot to Wagner/Africa Corps. All facts confirmed.
